channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Nvidia Scandal Raises China Stakes
item.description: Terry Haines, the Founder of Pangea Policy joined Bloomberg Open Interest to talk about how the Nvidia scandal could have consequences far beyond the company. Haines says congressional and law-enforcement investigations may take months, while the episode could strengthen calls to restrict chip sales to China. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Lumentum Slips on Deal Reaction; Fossil Group Rallies on Outlook | Stock Movers
item.description:
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- Shares of CoreWeave (CRWV) rallied in premarket trading after the compay eased fears about its debt-laden business during a high-stakes quarterly report, indicating that sales growth remains strong despite challenges facing the data center industry. The AI computing provider projected revenue of $13 billion to $13.3 billion this year. That exceeded its previous range of up to $13.2 billion and sailed past the $12.9 billion that Wall Street had predicted. - Shares of Lumentum Holdings (LITE) slipped ahead of the US market open. Marvell Technology’s (MRVL) plan to double down on AI through a blockbuster $115 billion acquisition of Lumentum is getting a lukewarm early verdict from investment experts who bet on deals. - Shares of Fossil Group (FOSL) rallied after the company raised its full-year sales outlook after posting quarterly growth sooner than expected. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta’s Head of Infrastructure, Engineering to Depart in 2027
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc.’s longtime infrastructure chief will leave the company in early 2027, a major leadership change as it continues to invest hundreds of billions of dollars in artificial intelligence and the data centers needed to support it.
item.dc:creator: Riley Griffin

item.title: Nvidia Is Playing Out Like a Greek Tragedy, Says Seaport's Goldberg
item.description: Jay Goldberg, Seaport senior analyst, says Nvidia would lose its identity without CEO Jensen Huang. Goldberg says the risk of Huang being removed is significant. He speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Helsing Unveils AI Military Software to Challenge Palantir
item.description: Helsing Gmbh, a German dronemaker, released a platform that uses artificial intelligence to help military units process data from the field more quickly, creating a new European challenger to US-based Palantir Technologies Inc.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Sealy

item.title: Anthropic IPO Said to Be Multiple Times Oversubscribed
item.description: Anthropic's IPO has drawn multiple times the orders for the shares available, according to people familiar with the matter, as demand accelerates for potentially the biggest first-time share sale ever. Bailey Lipschultz reports on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Elon Musk’s AI Chatbot Grok Sexualized These Teens’ Childhood Photos
item.description: The images are nearly impossible to erase. Now, a growing number of victims are pushing to hold Elon Musk’s xAI accountable.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra S. Levine

item.title: Nvidia Gets Rare Downgrade as Baird Raises CEO Uncertainities
item.description: Wall Street sentiment toward Nvidia Corp. is starting to crack, as an investigation into Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy is sowing doubt over the artificial intelligence chipmaker’s prospects.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Vlastelica

item.title: Take-Two CEO Zelnick: AI Wont Kill Gaming Jobs
item.description: Take-Two Interactive Chairman & CEO Strauss Zelnick says artificial intelligence will transform the video game industry, but he doesn't believe It will lead to fewer jobs. He says technology ultimately needs to serve one goal: make great entertainment. Zelnick sits down with David Rubenstein on this week’s episode of The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations. This interview was recorded October 19 in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Take-Two’s Zelnick Traded Movies for ‘Grand Theft Auto’ Games
item.description:
Take-Two Interactive Chairman & CEO Strauss Zelnick reflects on his career in entertainment, from becoming president of 20th Century Fox to leaving the movie and television business for the emerging video game industry. He also discusses how he helped transform Take-Two into one of the biggest companies in gaming. Zelnick sits down with David Rubenstein on this week’s episode of The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations. This interview was recorded October 19 in New York.
(Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Is Latest Big Swing for Take-Two CEO’s Video Game Empire
item.description: Take-Two Interactive Software Inc. Chief Executive Officer Strauss Zelnick wanted to run a Hollywood studio when he was a kid.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Palmeri

item.title: Nvidia Is Core Part AI-Basket of Stocks, Emanuel Says
item.description: Julian Emanuel, Evercore ISI chief equity strategist and quantitative strategist, says Nvidia is a core part of their basket of AI stocks. He also expects the Anthropic IPO to go smoothly. He speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: SAP Touts AI Tools, But Fails to Disclose Numbers to Measure Results
item.description: The software company hasn’t disclosed many metrics to show whether its AI effort is paying off
item.dc:creator: Christina Kyriasoglou

item.title: Utah-Based Startup Raises $500 Million for Modular AI Data Center
item.description: Torus, an energy-storage startup, said it raised $500 million in funding to help launch a new shipping container-sized product that combines batteries with artificial-intelligence computing.
item.dc:creator: Mark Chediak

item.title: Anthropic’s Mythos AI Looking for Cyber Flaws in Energy Systems
item.description: Some power companies are using cybersecurity technology from Anthropic PBC after spending months urging US government officials and the artificial intelligence company to help them access the company’s powerful AI models in order to help fend off hackers.
item.dc:creator: Julia Amann, Emma Haidar and Shirin Ghaffary

item.title: Citi’s Aganga on AI, Markets and Inflation
item.description: Olaolu Aganga of Citi says strong earnings and attractive valuations continue to support US stocks despite recent volatility. She discusses the long-term AI investment cycle, opportunities in cybersecurity and critical metals, and why AI productivity gains are still ahead. Aganga also warns inflation could remain hotter than expected, pushing rates higher and favoring shorter-duration fixed income and gold. She speaks with Anna Edwards on Bloomberg Brief. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Stocks Face Tug-of-War as Anthropic, CoreWeave Lift Hopes
item.description: The AI trade is so massive that its friends and foes increasingly find support on the same day.
item.dc:creator: Kristine Owram

item.title: Airbnb Is Building Its Own AI Travel Agent, Co-Founder Says
item.description: Airbnb Co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer Nathan Blecharczyk says the company is developing its own specialized AI travel agent that will eventually be able to book both on and off Airbnb’s platform. In an interview with Bloomberg’s Francine Lacqua on “The Pulse”, he spoke about how AI is transforming Airbnb, the company’s return to growth, regulation and housing in Europe, and the shift in travel beyond major cities. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Kai-Fu Lee Questions Soaring AI Valuations
item.description: AI pioneer Kai-Fu Lee discusses whether trillion-dollar AI valuations can be justified, the risks of circular funding, and the impact of cheaper Chinese and open-source models. The Sinovation Ventures Chairman and CEO and 01.AI CEO also explains why businesses need to reinvent themselves around AI, and why Europe’s biggest opportunity may be in AI applications rather than foundation models. Lee appeared on “The Pulse with Francine Lacqua”. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CoreWeave Shares Soar After AI Computing Firm Eases Debt Fears
item.description: CoreWeave Inc. shares soared after the AI computing supplier eased fears about its debt-laden business and signaled that sales growth remains strong despite the many headwinds facing the data center boom.
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass and Brody Ford
